title: “Go for exhaustion” tried to be the new life mantra
summary:
The spiciest take was @the_wilderless flat-out declaring: “Exhaustion is the most important part of human development,” and claiming it’s basically ignored by developmental psychology. The post (“The Only Thing to Do”) frames the move as committing hard to your current reality—so hard you *exhaust* it—rather than trying to hack your way around discomfort.

The mini-arc: River (@the_wilderless) drops the essay (June 11), then doubles down with the “exhaustion” thesis. A couple people bite: @sensefulronin pushes back with the only real question (“Can we truly exhaust the suck?”) and notes it doesn’t feel accelerationist; @alex_with_ease says it’s an avoided truth they had to face. The peak is basically quote-tweet affirmation—@bierlingm lifting the line “go all in on exactly where you are,” @m_ashcroft calling it a hard-hitter, and @WystanTBS turning it into a poetic battle cry (“Trackless as birds soaring sky!”). River even tries to meme it into a quote card, but it doesn’t spread.

Then it just… stops. No real debate, no second-order insights, and the “thread” gets padded by unrelated semantic-matches (tardigrade jokes, “Never Goon,” honey meme). Why care? It’s a clean snapshot of how Twitter turns a potentially provocative idea (exhaustion-as-growth) into aesthetic agreement and repostable slogans—great if you want a mantra, useless if you wanted an argument.
